messages:
alex: quick heads-up — noticed steady memory growth in kv-cache on canary with long-context llama2-70b runs (12k+ tokens). not a single crash but +2.2GB over ~30 minutes. attaching small profile snippet below.

alex: pprof top-ish:
```
kv_cache.total: 2.8GB
  slab0 (64B blocks): 200MB used, 300MB free (lots of tiny holes)
  slab1 (512B blocks): 1.0GB used, 400MB free
  slab2 (4KB blocks): 1.6GB used, 100MB free
fragmentation_estimate: ~28%
long_context_kv_hits: high (most keys live in slab2)
```

priya: is this from the new batching pattern or earlier?
ajex: (typo) alex: looks correlated with longer prefixes + repeated decode steps. not seen on shorter chats.

jordan: can you paste the eviction stats? i want to see paging/evict churn.
alex: eviction events per minute: 0.2 on canary (low), but free hole count ++ over time. seems like allocator is leaving unusable leftover fragments rather than coalescing.

sam: hmm — sounds like slab internal fragmentation rather than GC pressure. did we change block size thresholds in last deploy?

maria: we shipped the allocator tuning patch last week that adds a 512B slab for medium KV entries. may be interaction with variable-length cache entries.

priya: proposal: try a sampling-based fragment metric instead of global free %. sample N random slab pages, compute hole density and avg hole size. triggers compaction when hole_density > watermark AND avg_hole_size > X. cheaper than full scan.

jordan: +1. We previously used global free% which misses many small unusable pockets. sampling would detect clustering. what sample rate?

priya: thinking reservoir sample of 1024 slots every 5 minutes. light-weight and incremental. also add exponential backoff on compaction if recent compactions failed to reduce fragmentation (avoid thundering).

perf-bot: perf regression detected on canary: kv_compaction_rate +25% (p95 latency unaffected).

sam: good catch. also consider watermark hysteresis: high watermark (60%) => compaction, low watermark (35%) => stop. prevents flip-flop.

alex: we should simulate with the frag-sim tool before rolling. i ran quick sim: using sample-trigger + 60/35 watermarks reduced peak mem by ~400MB on synthetic long-context trace, but compaction CPU went up ~12% during events.

maria: tradeoff accepted if we schedule compaction on low-load windows or use low-priority bg threads. we could also prioritize compaction of slabs with highest avg hole size first.

jordan: another axis: adaptive block sizing for long-lived keys. if a key gets rewritten often and grows, try to migrate it to larger blocks proactively (cheap bump copy) to reduce future splits.

priya: that is cool but complex. start with sampling + watermarks + hysteresis + prioritize large-hole slabs. then measure.

alex: experimental plan:
- implement reservoir sampler + frag metric (priya)
- add compaction watermarks 60/35 + hysteresis (sam)
- compaction priority sort by avg_hole_size (jordan)
- schedule compaction as bg low-prio thread, respect CPU quota (maria)
- run canary for 48h with long-context trace and compare mem & CPU (alex)

maria: i'll add a dashboard for sampled frag metric + compaction ops per slab and CPU. put alerts if compaction CPU > 20% sustained.

perf-bot: added perf job kv-frag-sampling-canary to CI, will run nightly.

sam: small nit: when compaction moves blocks, ensure we propagate KV cache pointers atomically to avoid stale pointers during decode. we have helper move_and_swap() in allocator; reuse it.

jordan: also log pre/post free% and avg_hole_size for each compaction event for offline analysis. keep logs as metrics not full dumps.

alex: thanks — i'll open PR with sampler + metric and a small sim harness (will include config knobs for sample size and watermarks). linking here when ready.

priya: one more note: for very long contexts we may want to evict rare prefixes earlier (freq-based eviction), combine with compaction to keep working set small. future follow-up.

maria: okay. next sync in #eng-runtime on Monday to review canary numbers. :thumbsup:

alex: assigning todos in the PR description. thanks all.
